title: The explicit two-term action complex
statement: Let A be a ring and G a topological group. On discrete continuous A-linear G-representations [def-exc-discrete-modules-category], fix tau in G. Define K(M) to have M in degrees 0 and 1, the zero module in every degree at least 2, and differential rho_M(tau)-id in degree 0 and zero elsewhere. A coefficient morphism acts by its underlying linear map in degrees 0 and 1 and by zero elsewhere. This is a functor to nonnegative cochain complexes of A-modules, with identity linear equivalences in the two nonzero degrees.

source.place: First paragraph, definition of the two-term complexes and their functoriality

proof.text: Construct the graded objects using M,M,PUnit,PUnit,... and use CochainComplex.of with the only potentially nonzero differential rho(tau)-id. Consecutive differentials compose to zero because one is zero.

Define coefficient maps by the original linear map in degrees 0 and 1. Equivariance gives commutation with rho(tau)-id, and the other chain-map equations are zero equations. Identities and composition hold degreewise. Identity linear equivalences identify degrees 0 and 1 with M; PUnit is a zero module in all higher degrees.
